title: Dengue infection (symptomatic)
recommended_action: Consider dengue as a probable diagnosis in patients presenting with the listed clinical conditions after the specified incubation period.

source.title: NATIONAL GUIDELINE FOR CLINICAL MANAGEMENT OF DENGUE

evidence.passage:
Symptoms develop after an incubation period of 4-7 days (range 3-14 days) and symptomatic patients may have one of the following conditions:
      •   Undifferentiated fever
      •  DF
      •  DHF
      •  Expanded dengue syndrome (rare)

title: Classical Dengue Fever (DF)
recommended_action: Consider diagnosis of classical dengue fever and monitor for complications such as hemorrhage

source.title: NATIONAL GUIDELINE FOR CLINICAL MANAGEMENT OF DENGUE

evidence.passage: A proportion of patients infected with dengue virus develop classical dengue fever characterized by high fever, severe headache, retro-orbital pain, myalgia, arthralgia and rashes. Leucopenia and thrombocytopenia are usually observed.
The body temperature is usually between 39 °C and 40 °C (102° F to 104° F).

title: Dengue rash patterns
recommended_action: Recognize rash as a possible manifestation of acute dengue infection

source.title: NATIONAL GUIDELINE FOR CLINICAL MANAGEMENT OF DENGUE

evidence.passage: Undifferentiated macular or maculopapular rash may occur over the face, thorax, abdomen, and extremities during the acute phase of dengue. The rash is typically macular or maculopapular and may be associated with pruritus.

Convalescent rash is characterized by confluent erythematous eruption with sparing areas of normal skin. It is often pruritic. The rash typically occurs within one to two days of defervescence and lasts one to five days.

title: Warning signs indicating severe dengue

requires_any.note: ≥3 episodes in 1 hr or ≥4 in 6 hrs
pleural effusion, ascites, or pericardial effusion
progressive increase in at least 2 consecutive measurements 6 hours apart

recommended_action: Promptly refer for higher level care and initiate close monitoring for shock

source.title: NATIONAL GUIDELINE FOR CLINICAL MANAGEMENT OF DENGUE

evidence.passage: Warning signs of dengue fever: • Intense continuous abdominal pain or pain when palpating abdomen • Persistent vomiting (≥3 episodes in 1 hr or ≥4 in 6 hrs) • Fluid accumulation (pleural effusion, ascites, or pericardial effusion) • Mucosal bleeding (gums, nose, vagina [metrorrhagia or hypermenorrhea], kidney [macroscopic hematuria]) • Altered mental status (irritability, drowsiness, Glasgow Coma Scale score <15) • Hepatomegaly (≥2cm below costal margin) • Progressive increase of the haematocrit (in at least 2 consecutive measurements taken 6 hours apart)

title: Monitoring for plasma leakage in DHF
recommended_action: Serial haematocrit measurements every 6 hours during critical phase to detect rising haematocrit

source.title: NATIONAL GUIDELINE FOR CLINICAL MANAGEMENT OF DENGUE

evidence.passage: Progressive increase of the haematocrit (in at least 2 consecutive measurements taken 6 hours apart)

title: Phases of Dengue Haemorrhagic Fever (DHF)
recommended_action: Expect three clinical phases: febrile, critical (leakage), and convalescent; monitor accordingly

source.title: NATIONAL GUIDELINE FOR CLINICAL MANAGEMENT OF DENGUE

evidence.passage: Clinical course of DHF is stereotypic and consists of three phases: • Febrile phase • Critical phase (leakage phase) • Convalescent phase

title: CBC and NS1/Anti‑Dengue Antibody at first visit
recommended_action: Obtain complete blood count (CBC) and NS‑1 antigen/anti‑dengue antibody test at the first clinical encounter, timing based on day of presentation

source.title: NATIONAL GUIDELINE FOR CLINICAL MANAGEMENT OF DENGUE

evidence.passage: CBC and NS-1 Ag/ Anti-Dengue Ab should be done in all suspected dengue patients at their first visit depending on the day of presentation.

title: Interpretation of CBC parameters for dengue severity
recommended_action: Assess WBC count, neutrophil‑lymphocyte ratio, and platelet count to gauge disease phase and severity

source.title: NATIONAL GUIDELINE FOR CLINICAL MANAGEMENT OF DENGUE

evidence.passage: WBC counts: Leucopenia is common in both adults and children with DF (Level 1) and has an important diagnostic implication in early period. The change in total white cell count (≤5000 cells/mm3) and ratio of neutrophils to lymphocyte (neutrophils <lymphocytes) is useful to predict the critical period of plasma leakage (Level 6).
NLR (Neutrophil Lymphocyte ratio) <2 strongly correlates with low platelets indicating severity of disease and reversal of NLR >2 correlates with improvement of disease (Level 6).
Thrombocytopenia (<100,000/mm3) usually precedes/accompanies plasma leakage.

title: Haematocrit monitoring during critical phase
recommended_action: Measure haematocrit at least twice daily (more frequently if possible) to detect a rise >10% (onset of plasma leakage) or >20% (established leakage) and guide fluid management

source.title: NATIONAL GUIDELINE FOR CLINICAL MANAGEMENT OF DENGUE

evidence.passage: Haematocrit (Hct): Haemotacrit is most important tool in diagnosing and guiding effective treatment of dengue patient(Level 5). Approximately 5-10% increase in Hct may occur due to high fever, anorexia and vomiting. A sudden rise in haematocrit is observed simultaneously or shortly after the drop in platelet count. Rising haematocrit more than 10 % indicates starting plasma lekage and rising haematocrit by 20% from the baseline indicates established plasma leakage.

During plasma leakage period Hct should be monitored at least twice daily and more frequently considering the clinical scenario, If facilities available. Bedside haematocrit is suggested in admitted patients.

title: Dengue NS1 antigen test
recommended_action: Perform NS1 antigen test (rapid or ELISA) to detect dengue early

source.title: NATIONAL GUIDELINE FOR CLINICAL MANAGEMENT OF DENGUE

evidence.passage: The Dengue NS1 antigen usually positive on first day of illness.
This antigen test may become negative from 4-5 days of illness.

title: Dengue IgM/IgG antibody test (MAC ELISA or rapid)
recommended_action: Perform IgM/IgG antibody test to confirm dengue after day 5

source.title: NATIONAL GUIDELINE FOR CLINICAL MANAGEMENT OF DENGUE

evidence.passage: Anti-dengue IgM can be detected after 5 days of the onset of fever and reaches highest level after 7 days of fever.
In primary dengue infection- anti-dengue IgM will be detected earlier than IgG which (IgG) will appear on the 9th or 10th day of illness.

title: Dengue RT‑PCR (viral RNA detection)
recommended_action: Order RT‑PCR to confirm dengue infection within first 5 days of symptoms

source.title: NATIONAL GUIDELINE FOR CLINICAL MANAGEMENT OF DENGUE

evidence.passage: Dengue diagnosis is confirmed by detecting DEN viral RNA using reverse transcriptase polymerase chain reaction (RT‑PCR; This test is usually positive within 5 days of onset of symptoms.

title: Dengue virus isolation (research)
recommended_action: Collect serum, plasma or leukocytes for virus isolation in cell culture (research use only)

source.title: NATIONAL GUIDELINE FOR CLINICAL MANAGEMENT OF DENGUE

evidence.passage: Dengue virus isolation in cell culture (Vero, C6/36 cell lines) done from serum, plasma and leucocytes is the most definitive test for dengue infection, which can be usually accomplished in majority of cases if the sample is taken in the first five days of onset of symptoms.

title: Serum AST and ALT measurement
recommended_action: Measure serum AST (SGOT) and ALT (SGPT) to assess liver involvement; note that AST is usually higher than ALT and marked elevations correlate with severe dengue

source.title: NATIONAL GUIDELINE FOR CLINICAL MANAGEMENT OF DENGUE

evidence.passage: Serum AST (SGOT) and ALT (SGPT): Transaminases are commonly abnormal in dengue fever where classically AST is more than ALT. Elevated aspartate aminotransferase levels were strongly associated with severe dengue.
In Classical Dengue fever AST/ ALT may be slightly raised (2-5 times of upper limit of normal) but in dengue haemorrhagic fever ALT and AST may be 5 to 15 times the upper limit of normal.

title: Serum Albumin measurement
recommended_action: Measure serum albumin; a level <3.5 gm/dl indicates plasma leakage

source.title: NATIONAL GUIDELINE FOR CLINICAL MANAGEMENT OF DENGUE

evidence.passage: Serum Albumin <3.5 gm/dl indicates plasma leakage.

title: Renal function tests (Serum Creatinine/BUN)
recommended_action: Check serum creatinine and blood urea nitrogen as they may be elevated in prolonged shock

source.title: NATIONAL GUIDELINE FOR CLINICAL MANAGEMENT OF DENGUE

evidence.passage: Serum Creatinine/Blood urea nitrogen (BUN) may be elevated in prolonged shock.

title: Serum Electrolytes
recommended_action: Assess electrolytes; hyponatremia is frequently observed

source.title: NATIONAL GUIDELINE FOR CLINICAL MANAGEMENT OF DENGUE

evidence.passage: Serum Electrolyte: Hyponatremia is frequently observed in DHF/DSS

title: Venous Blood Gas (VBG) analysis
recommended_action: Perform VBG to detect metabolic acidosis which is frequently found in prolonged shock

source.title: NATIONAL GUIDELINE FOR CLINICAL MANAGEMENT OF DENGUE

evidence.passage: VBG (venous blood gas analysis): Metabolic acidosis is frequently found in cases with prolonged shock

title: Random Blood Sugar (RBS)
recommended_action: Check RBS; may be low in DSS

source.title: NATIONAL GUIDELINE FOR CLINICAL MANAGEMENT OF DENGUE

evidence.passage: RBS may be low in DSS

title: Serum Calcium
recommended_action: Measure serum calcium; hypocalcaemia (corrected for hypoalbuminemia) has been observed

source.title: NATIONAL GUIDELINE FOR CLINICAL MANAGEMENT OF DENGUE

evidence.passage: Serum calcium: Hypocalcaemia (corrected for hypoalbuminemia) has been observed in DHF.

title: Coagulation profile
recommended_action: Assess aPTT, PT and TT; aPTT prolonged in ~50% and PT in ~33% of DHF cases, TT prolonged in severe cases

source.title: NATIONAL GUIDELINE FOR CLINICAL MANAGEMENT OF DENGUE

evidence.passage: Assays of coagulation and fibrinolytic factors show reduction in DSS cases. Activated Partial thromboplastin time (aPPT) and prothrombin time (PT) are prolonged in about half and one third of DHF cases respectively. Thrombin time (TT) is also prolonged in severe cases.

title: Chest X‑Ray
recommended_action: Obtain chest X‑ray to detect pleural effusion indicating fluid accumulation

source.title: NATIONAL GUIDELINE FOR CLINICAL MANAGEMENT OF DENGUE

evidence.passage: Chest X-Ray: Pleural effusion on X-ray in dengue indicates fluid accumulation.

title: Ultrasonography
recommended_action: Perform ultrasound to detect pleural effusions or ascites for objective evidence of capillary plasma leakage

source.title: NATIONAL GUIDELINE FOR CLINICAL MANAGEMENT OF DENGUE

evidence.passage: Ultrasonography: To detect pleural effusions or ascites, it is essential to obtain objective evidence of selective capillary plasma leaking into the chest and abdominal cavities.

title: Urine R/M/E
recommended_action: Examine urine for albuminuria or hematuria

source.title: NATIONAL GUIDELINE FOR CLINICAL MANAGEMENT OF DENGUE

evidence.passage: Urine R/M/E: Albuminuria/Hematuria may be present

title: Exclusion tests for other infections
recommended_action: Perform ICT or microscopy for malaria and blood culture to exclude enteric fever

source.title: NATIONAL GUIDELINE FOR CLINICAL MANAGEMENT OF DENGUE

evidence.passage: Other tests might be done to exclude other diagnosis such as ICT for malaria, microscopy for malaria, Blood culture to exclude enteric fever.

title: Cardiac evaluation (ECG, Echocardiography, Troponin I, CK‑MB)
recommended_action: Order ECG, echocardiography, troponin I and CK‑MB if myocarditis is suspected

source.title: NATIONAL GUIDELINE FOR CLINICAL MANAGEMENT OF DENGUE

evidence.passage: ECG, Echocardiography, Troponin I, CK-MB if myocarditis is suspected.

title: CSF analysis
recommended_action: Perform CSF examination if dengue encephalitis is suspected

source.title: NATIONAL GUIDELINE FOR CLINICAL MANAGEMENT OF DENGUE

evidence.passage: CSF: In dengue encephalitis.

title: Baseline laboratory investigations for suspected dengue

requires_all.note: patient presented within 5 days of fever

recommended_action: Obtain CBC, haematocrit, Dengue NS1 antigen, SGOT, SGPT at first consultation to establish baseline.

source.title: NATIONAL GUIDELINE FOR CLINICAL MANAGEMENT OF DENGUE

evidence.passage: Within 5 days: CBC, Haematocrit, Dengue NS1 antigen, SGOT, SGPT
These tests should be done during first consultation to get the baseline characteristics like Haematocrit and complete blood count if the patient presented within 5 days of fever.

title: Follow‑up laboratory monitoring when DHF is suspected
recommended_action: Perform daily CBC, haematocrit, and other labs from the first afebrile day and continue daily while DHF is suspected; stop daily labs when platelet count reaches ≥ 50,000/mm³.

source.title: NATIONAL GUIDELINE FOR CLINICAL MANAGEMENT OF DENGUE

evidence.passage: Follow up testing may be done on 1st afebrile day, but should be done daily once DHF is suspected.
Once the platelet count begins to rise and reaches ≥ 50,000/mm3,daily lab evaluations may be discontinued.

title: Point‑of‑care ultrasound for plasma leakage assessment
recommended_action: Perform bedside POC ultrasound to evaluate gallbladder wall thickening, hepato‑renal pouch fluid, right pleural fluid, and pelvic fluid for objective diagnosis of plasma leakage.

source.title: NATIONAL GUIDELINE FOR CLINICAL MANAGEMENT OF DENGUE

evidence.passage: Point of care ultrasonography is not essential to manage dengue patient but it has now evolved into an important and reliable method of diagnosing plasma leakage objectively in clinically suspected DHF patients.

Main areas: Gallbladder - gallbladder wall thickening and appearance of para cholecystic fluid; Fluid in the hepato-renal pouch; Fluid in right pleural cavity; Fluid in the pelvis (recto vesical pouch)

title: Haematocrit monitoring frequency
recommended_action: Monitor haematocrit at least every 3 hours (or more frequently) in severe dengue, especially with shock.

source.title: NATIONAL GUIDELINE FOR CLINICAL MANAGEMENT OF DENGUE

evidence.passage: Even in severe dengue especially with shock haematocrit to be monitored 3 hourly or more frequently is crucial for management.

title: Probable Dengue Case Definition
recommended_action: Classify patient as probable dengue case

source.title: NATIONAL GUIDELINE FOR CLINICAL MANAGEMENT OF DENGUE

evidence.passage: Probable Case: Acute febrile illness with serological diagnosis.

title: Basic Outpatient Investigations for Dengue by Day of Illness

when.note: day of illness up to day 5

variants.action: Perform CBC and NS1 antigen test
Perform CBC and Dengue antibody test

recommended_action: Order investigations according to day of illness

source.title: NATIONAL GUIDELINE FOR CLINICAL MANAGEMENT OF DENGUE

evidence.passage: Basic investigations depend on day of illness. CBC and NS1 Ag up to day 5 and CBC and Dengue Antibody from day 6 onward will support the diagnosis.

title: Outpatient Assessment Checklist for Dengue
symptoms_or_prerequisites: patient presenting with acute febrile illness
recommended_action: Collect history items: date of fever onset, last fever episode, oral intake, warning signs, diarrhoea, bleeding, mental status changes, urine output, drug history, comorbidities.

source.title: NATIONAL GUIDELINE FOR CLINICAL MANAGEMENT OF DENGUE

evidence.passage: Stepwise approach on outpatient management on dengue History: •  Date of onset of fever/ illness •  Date and time of last episode of fever •   Oral intake •  Warning signs •   Diarrhoea •   Bleeding including menstrual bleeding •  Change in mental status /seizure /dizziness •   Urine output (frequency, volume and time of last voiding) •  Other important relevant histories: drug history, comorbidities.

title: Dengue Without Warning Signs Criteria
symptoms_or_prerequisites: two or more of: nausea, vomiting, rash, aches and pains, positive tourniquet test, leucopenia
recommended_action: Classify as dengue without warning signs

source.title: NATIONAL GUIDELINE FOR CLINICAL MANAGEMENT OF DENGUE

evidence.passage: Dengue without warning signs: Fever (2-7 days) with two or more of the followings; nausea, vomiting, rash, aches and pains, positive tourniquet tests, or leucopenia (WBC <5000/mm3)

title: Dengue With Warning Signs Criteria
recommended_action: Classify as dengue with warning signs

source.title: NATIONAL GUIDELINE FOR CLINICAL MANAGEMENT OF DENGUE

evidence.passage: Dengue with warning signs: Dengue fever with any one of the warning signs.

title: Complete blood count and haematocrit
recommended_action: Order CBC and haematocrit to assess for thrombocytopenia and hemoconcentration.

source.title: NATIONAL GUIDELINE FOR CLINICAL MANAGEMENT OF DENGUE

evidence.passage: •  CBC and Hct

title: NS1 antigen test
recommended_action: Perform NS-1 test for early dengue diagnosis.

source.title: NATIONAL GUIDELINE FOR CLINICAL MANAGEMENT OF DENGUE

evidence.passage: •  NS-1

title: Liver enzymes (SGPT/SGOT)
recommended_action: Measure SGPT and SGOT to monitor hepatic involvement.

source.title: NATIONAL GUIDELINE FOR CLINICAL MANAGEMENT OF DENGUE

evidence.passage: •  SGPT/SGOT

title: C-reactive protein (CRP) level 4
recommended_action: Obtain CRP (level 4) as part of dengue assessment.

source.title: NATIONAL GUIDELINE FOR CLINICAL MANAGEMENT OF DENGUE

evidence.passage: •  CRP (level 4)

title: Admission for high‑risk patients
recommended_action: Consider hospital admission even without other severity criteria.

source.title: NATIONAL GUIDELINE FOR CLINICAL MANAGEMENT OF DENGUE

evidence.passage: Patients at high risk for more severe disease and its complications may need admission even without the above criteria.
  Pregnant women
  Elderly
  Obesity
  Patients on anticoagulants
  Age <1 year or >65 years

title: Home management for dengue patients without warning signs or high‑risk conditions
recommended_action: Provide home‑based care with regular follow‑up and assessment

source.title: NATIONAL GUIDELINE FOR CLINICAL MANAGEMENT OF DENGUE

evidence.passage: Patients without warning signs or coexisting conditions or social risk should get home based care through a register of dengue patient.
Adequate physical rest in comfortable clothing, and preferably under a mosquito net

title: Hydration recommendations for dengue home care
recommended_action: Ensure oral fluid intake ≈2400 ml/24 h (or 2 ml/kg/h if weight < 50 kg) spread across the day; use ORS, coconut water, fruit juices or soup with electrolytes

source.title: NATIONAL GUIDELINE FOR CLINICAL MANAGEMENT OF DENGUE

evidence.passage: Ensure adequate oral fluid intake of around 2400 ml for 24 hours (if the body weight is less than 50kg, give fluids as 2ml/kg/hour for 24 hours) and it is better to spread this amount of fluid across the day.

title: Paracetamol dosing limit in dengue
symptoms_or_prerequisites: home management or any dengue patient
recommended_action: Do not exceed 3 g/day of paracetamol (60 mg/kg/24 h in child)

medication.name: Paracetamol
medication.instructions: Tepid sponging for fever; warn that fever may not fully settle with paracetamol and advise not to take excess

source.title: NATIONAL GUIDELINE FOR CLINICAL MANAGEMENT OF DENGUE

evidence.passage: Do not exceed 3 gm/day of paracetamol. (60mg/kg/24hrs in child)

title: Criteria for inpatient admission of dengue patients
recommended_action: Admit for inpatient management

source.title: NATIONAL GUIDELINE FOR CLINICAL MANAGEMENT OF DENGUE

evidence.passage: Present WS  Present  Derange VS Reduced UOP  WBC: decreasing Platelet ≤100x109/L Increasing Hct: Leaking Decreasing Hct: Bleeding High risk. Inpatient management

title: Dietary recommendations for dengue patients at home
recommended_action: Encourage light and nutritious food if appetite is good; if appetite is poor, do not force feeding and ensure adequate fluid intake; avoid red/brown colored foods and beverages.

source.title: NATIONAL GUIDELINE FOR CLINICAL MANAGEMENT OF DENGUE

evidence.passage: If the appetite is good, patients encouraged to take light and nutritious food.
If the patient’s appetite is poor, forced feeding should not be done, as taking adequate amounts of liquid is sufficient during illness.
It is advisable to avoid red/ brown (i.e. dark) colored food (red dragon fruit, beet root)/ beverages to avoid confusion with blood-stained vomitus/ melaena)

title: Use of anti-emetics and acid suppressants in dengue
recommended_action: Administer anti-emetics and PPI/H2 receptor blockers if necessary.

source.title: NATIONAL GUIDELINE FOR CLINICAL MANAGEMENT OF DENGUE

evidence.passage: Anti-emetics and PPI/H2 receptor blockers if necessary.

title: Avoidance of NSAIDs, steroids and certain antithrombotics

variants.action: Temporarily withhold these drugs and seek expert opinion if they are necessary.

recommended_action: Avoid all NSAIDs (including COX-2 inhibitors) and steroids; temporarily withhold warfarin, aspirin, clopidogrel & dipyridamole in long‑term users.

source.title: NATIONAL GUIDELINE FOR CLINICAL MANAGEMENT OF DENGUE

evidence.passage: Avoid all NSAIDS (including COX-2 inhibitors) and steroids.
Temporally withhold warfarin, aspirin, clopidogrel & dipyridamole, in patients who take these on long term basis. Take expert opinion where these drugs are necessary.

title: CBC monitoring schedule for home‑managed dengue patients
recommended_action: Review CBC daily; first CBC at least on the beginning of day 3 of fever/illness (preferably with SGOT and SGPT). Continue follow‑up until afebrile for 24‑48 h with stable clinical parameters.

source.title: NATIONAL GUIDELINE FOR CLINICAL MANAGEMENT OF DENGUE

evidence.passage: Review daily with CBC. First CBC should be done at least at the beginning of the third day of fever/illness (preferably with SGOT and SGPT).
These patients should be followed up until the patient become afebrile for 24-48 hours with stable clinical parameters.

title: Warning signs for immediate return or hospitalization

requires_any.value: clinical deterioration with settling of fever
bleeding tendency (abnormal vaginal bleeding, blood vomiting, black tarry stool, nose or gum bleeding)
reduced urine output for last 4-6 hours (<150-200 ml/4-6 hours if weight ≥50 kg)

recommended_action: Advise patients to return to the hospital immediately if any of the listed warning signs develop.

source.title: NATIONAL GUIDELINE FOR CLINICAL MANAGEMENT OF DENGUE

evidence.passage: Advise patients to return to the hospital immediately, if they develop any of the following conditions: Clinical deterioration with settling of fever; Inability to tolerate oral fluids; Severe abdominal pain; Lethargy or irritability / restlessness
Bleeding tendency like abnormal vaginal bleeding, blood vomiting, black tarry stool, bleeding from nose and gum.
Reduced urine output for the last 4-6 hours (<150-200 ml/ 4-6 hours if weight is 50kg or more)
Cold and clammy extremities
Difficulty in breathing.
